newsitem.title: USA: Kraft says no recall of Toblerone chocolate in US.
newsitem.headline: Kraft says no recall of Toblerone chocolate in US.

text.p: U.S. food manufacturer Kraft Foods Inc, a unit of Philip Morris Cos Inc, will not recall Toblerone chocolate bars that contain gene-altered ingredients in the United States, despite a recall in Switzerland, a company official said Monday.
"This is much ado about nothing," said Michael Mudd, spokesman for Kraft in Northfield, Ill. "There's no recall in the U.S."

Swiss chocolate maker Kraft Jacobs Suchard said it began a recall of chocolate products in Switzerland after authorities in Berne last week discovered genetically-altered soy products at its production facility.
"This is purely a Swiss regulatory issue," Mudd said. "There is no health concern."
A final decision from Swiss authorities on the use of gene-altered soybean products is pending. A ruling could come as early as this week.
Both the U.S. Department of Agriculture and the Food and Drug Administration have said products with genetically-altered soybeans were safe for consumption.
Europe's Suchard has publicly stated it would use only non-modified soy products as long as they were available, but Mudd said no such statement had been made in the U.S.
Toblerone chocolate bars sold in the U.S. are manufactured in Europe, Mudd said.
